licence.notes: Card: Apache-2.0 "following Gemma 4". "Dataset rights remain separate". Base google/gemma-4-12B-it card: Apache-2.0. The card's evaluation dataset akhilaaa3/decision-bench says its scenarios were generated with Claude Opus 5 - Anthropic terms for those outputs are an open question if they were used in training.

jev_distillation.evidence: "nothing in it was trained on Jev output." (author note: "not affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by, or derived from TypeSafe AI or its Jev model"). The card has no training-data section; this is the author's statement, not an audit.

installer_policy.reason: Not in the union of the open JevBench board's top 10 by Capability Score and top 10 by Composite Score (board v1.7.43, 2026-10-10), so the one-command installer does not support it. Local install is available on request.
installer_policy.previous_reason: Apache-2.0 model and an explicit author statement that no Jev output was used. Open questions: training data is not described, and the evaluation dataset's Claude-generated content.

readout.notes: In-process: load_jev_omni(path) returns a classifier that answers noul, choice and score with calibrated probabilities (256-way head). The card's typed-decision interface maps to Jev's shape. No HTTP server in the BH run.
readout.portable_notes: No unmodified portable path: jev_omni.py L113–116 accepts a device argument but explicitly refuses anything except CUDA; inference L104 hard-codes torch.autocast("cuda"). https://huggingface.co/akhilaaa3/Jev-Omni/raw/c050d51354147985d13286cf4acf90f562f2c631/jev_omni.py . The trained 256-way head is in-process, so backend_agnostic=false. Loading the BF16 checkpoint into a different generic runtime would lose the native readout.

image_input.transport: Python API: predict(..., media='/path/to/file', modality='image'); no HTTP field documented
image_input.limits: UNVERIFIED for image size (card caps audio at 30 s and video at 16 frames)
image_input.installer_transport: POST /v1/multimodal with one data URL -> RGB PIL -> temporary PNG path -> author JevOmni.predict(modality=image).
image_input.installer_limits: One image, 2..256 distinct option descriptions; gateway limits also apply.
image_input.installer_notes: Source-derived unverified HTTP recipe; see catalog/IMAGE-RECIPES-V2.md.

variants.gpu_arch_min: UNVERIFIED (BH ran Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 and a 48 GB L40)

steps: pip install -r requirements.txt  (author; ffmpeg needed for audio)
path = snapshot_download('akhilaaa3/Jev-Omni'); sys.path.insert(0, path); from jev_omni import load_jev_omni

BH used an in-process adapter (no HTTP server): load_model.py builds Gemma4UnifiedTextModel from backbone/ in fp32 on CPU, casts nn.Linear weights to bf16, moves to CUDA, runs bf16 autocast, reads the 256-way head
A Jev-compatible endpoint needs our wrapper; not part of the BH recipe

variants.expected_speed: Not measured for this installer recipe. Historical published benchmark timings describe a separate runtime.
variants.notes: Files: fp32 backbone 13 shards (~50 GB) + base Gemma 4 12B multimodal components (23.9 GB, the author loader downloads them). Disk 74 GB is required because both are needed. The repo's unified/model.safetensors (23.9 GB, bf16) is not used by the BH loader and is excluded. VRAM min 40 from BH meta; recommended 48 (BH run 8 used a 48 GB L40 with the bf16 cast). head.pt and runtime_buffers.pt are loaded with weights_only=True (author loader); sha256.json and verification.json are included for checking. Host RAM provisioning estimate: pinned weight files sum to 71.553 GB; ×1.25 loader/runtime allowance rounded up to 4 GB gives 92 GB. This is not a measured peak; FP32 initialization or duplicate weight buffers may require more. Installer recipe is source-derived and unverified; this executable runtime was not benchmarked. See catalog/IMAGE-RECIPES-V2.md for modifications and dependency provenance.
